title: SOC2 prep scratchpad - Elena Garcia
content:
Purpose / context:
- Personal scratchpad for SOC2 Type 1/2 prep. Not final - collecting notes for control mapping and evidence collection.
- Focus areas: access management (SSO, RBAC), change mgmt (infra PRs, release approvals), monitoring/alerts, incident response, data encryption (at-rest/in-transit), vendor mgmt (third-party infra).

High-level risks we care about:
- Unauthorized access to user data in hosted API or customer VPCs (misconfigs, leaked creds).
- Inadequate change control leading to regressions (runtime/kernel config, model rollout).
- Insufficient logging/retention for investigations (esp private deployments where customer-managed infra interacts).
- Key management gaps for on-prem customers (HSM/KMS integration evidence).

Control mapping (working):
- CC6 (Access): SSO via Okta + SCIM provisioning + groups. Evidence: Okta export of group membership (monthly snapshot), SCIM provisioning logs, IAM policy docs. TODO: get Noah to export the SCIM audit for July-Oct.
- CC7 (Encryption): All customer data at-rest on disk encrypted via cloud provider CMKs; Redwood recommends own KMS for Private. Evidence: KMS key policy screenshots, terraform state showing kms_key_id. Gap: need rotation evidence for customer-managed keys.
- CC3 (Change mgmt): GH repo protected branches, required reviews, CI checks. Evidence: repo settings screenshot, PR approval history for last 6 months (scripted export). Gap: need documented emergency change process and approvals log.
- CC4 (Monitoring): Logging centralization -> ELK/Datadog. Evidence: alert runbook links, retention policy doc, sample alert page. Gap: need proof of retention meets 90-day requirement for infra logs.

Outstanding questions for auditors / SCEs:
- For Dedicated nodes: do we treat GPU pool autoscaling config changes as config vs code? How to show approval traces? (Slack threads + PRs?)
- Private deployments: auditor asked for network diagrams. Do we have a canonical diagram per customer template? (MAYA to follow up)

Evidence inventory (quick):
- Okta group export: CONF-SEC-OKTA-2024-10.csv (waiting)
- Terraform plan PRs: list from infra repo (script: tools/export-prs.sh) -> TODO run and attach
- Access logs: s3://redwood-logs/hosts/api-auth-logs/2024/ -> need redaction process note
- Incident runbooks: runbooks/incident-response.md (link in Confluence) -> update ownership lines (oncall rotation)
- Pen test report: pen-test-2023.pdf (security drive) -> check remediation evidence for findings 4/7

Control owner notes / action items:
- Noah: export SCIM/Okta logs and push to evidence bucket (due 2024-11-06)
- Maya: canonical network diagram for Private deployments + sample customer diagram (due 2024-11-09)
- Oliver: run export of PR approvals for last 6 months, include emergency change tags (due 2024-11-04)
- Elena (me): consolidate evidence list and draft one-pager for auditor (due 2024-11-12)

Quick draft language for control descriptions (very rough):
- "Access provisioning: All user accounts are provisioned via Okta SCIM. Access to production resources is restricted to role-based groups. Onboarding/offboarding are managed through HR->Okta workflow; periodic access reviews performed quarterly."
- "Change control: Code and config changes require PRs with 2 approvers and automated CI. Emergency changes require documented rollback plan and retrospective."

Notes / open items (brain dump):
- Need to capture evidence of quarterly access review (did we do Q2/Q3? Where recorded?).
- Who signs org attestation for vendor mgmt? Product ops or legal? Add to checklist.
- How to handle ephemeral infra accounts created by CI? Need mapping to control (are they service accounts with limited scope?). Create doc: service-account-inventory.md
- Confirm log retention policy: infra logs 90d, app logs 30d, audit logs 365d? (verify with Observability team).

Next steps (sprint-style):
1) Pull exports from Okta + GitHub (Noah, Oliver) - by 11/06
2) Draft control descriptions and collect screenshots (Elena) - by 11/12
3) Network diagrams + Private deployment template (Maya) - by 11/09
4) Runbook updates and evidence links in Confluence (assign bench owners) - ongoing

Random notes to self:
- Save copies of any redacted logs to evidence bucket with naming convention: SOC2/<control-id>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD
- Use JIRA ticket SOC2-CORE as canonical tracker for remediation tasks
- Remind infra team to sign off on rotation policy (email thread exists: #infra-ops)

End of scratchpad.
